s.n: Carpe diem Welsh rarebit on toast
s.note: Sharp Vermont cheddar sauce grilled on toast.
s.how: Melt the butter, stir in the flour, then whisk in the milk until thick. Take off the heat and stir in both mustards, the cheese and yolk until smooth. Toast the bread on one side, spread the cheese mix thickly on the other and grill until bubbling and spotted brown. Dust with cayenne and serve hot.

s.n: Food for worms pea and ham soup
s.note: Split peas slow-cooked with a smoky hock. We are food for worms lads.
s.how: Put the hock, peas, vegetables, bay leaves and water in a big pot and bring to the boil. Simmer gently, stirring now and then, until the peas collapse and the meat falls off the bone. Lift out the hock, shred the meat and stir it back in, then season. Serve with thick slices of the loaf.

m.n: Opening night roast chicken with bread sauce
m.note: Golden roast chicken with buttered peas.
m.how: Rub the chicken with butter and salt, stuff with lemon and thyme, and roast at 200C with the oiled potatoes around it. Warm the milk with the clove-studded onion and leave to infuse. Lift out the onion, stir in the breadcrumbs and a knob of butter and cook until thick. Rest the chicken, boil the peas and serve everything with the bread sauce.

m.note: Lamb mince under a cheddar mash crust.
m.how: Brown the mince in the oil, add the onion and carrot and cook until soft. Stir in the tomato paste and flour, then the stock and Worcestershire, and simmer until thick. Boil and mash the potatoes with the butter and milk. Spoon the filling into a dish, spread over the mash, scatter with cheddar and bake at 200C until golden.

w.n: O Captain apple pie with Vermont cheddar
w.note: Spiced apple pie with a wedge of sharp cheddar.
w.how: Line a 23cm pie dish with one sheet of pastry. Toss the apples with the sugar, flour, spices and lemon juice and pile them in, dotted with butter. Cover with the second sheet, crimp, cut steam holes and brush with egg. Bake at 190C until golden and bubbling, then cool a little. Serve warm with a wedge of cheddar.

d.note: Thick cocoa poured from a thermos.
d.how: Whisk the cocoa and sugar into a little of the milk to a paste. Heat the rest of the milk, whisk in the paste and chocolate and stir until smooth and steaming. Add the vanilla and pour into a hot thermos or mugs.
